meta.title: @yukino.js/sentry — Frontend Monitoring & Analytics
meta.description: A lightweight, framework-agnostic browser SDK that captures errors, performance and user behavior from page load — one init() call, reporting only to your own endpoint.

hero.subtitle: A lightweight browser SDK that captures errors, performance and user behavior from the moment your page loads — initialize with a single dsn, report to your own endpoint.

showcase.description: A real session from a visitor's browser, streamed to your endpoint as it happens. Errors arrive with everything around them: identity, breadcrumbs, device info, performance and screen replay.
showcase.caption: One init() call streams every event above — no instrumentation added to your business code.

features.description: Error capture, performance metrics, behavior analytics, offline resilience and extension points — all from a single init() call, reported to your own endpoint.

errorCapture.title: Full error capture
errorCapture.description: Runtime errors, failed resource loads, unhandled rejections, console.error, failed XHR/fetch and React/Vue errors — enriched with breadcrumbs, identity and device context, deduplicated and batch-aggregated automatically, with the seconds before a failure replayed from a rolling screen record.

journeyTracking.title: Declarative journey tracking
journeyTracking.description: Page views with dwell time, clicks and element exposure duration via yukino-sentry-* attributes — behavior analytics without touching business logic.

webVitals.title: Web Vitals & timing
webVitals.description: LCP, FCP, CLS, INP and TTFB plus first-screen paint, navigation and resource timing, long tasks and memory — collected from real visits via PerformanceObserver.

whiteScreenReplay.title: White-screen detection
whiteScreenReplay.description: Viewport sampling detects pages that never render, including a skeleton-screen baseline mode — a blank page reports itself instead of failing silently.

offlineResilient.title: Built for bad networks
offlineResilient.description: Events batch and flush via sendBeacon or fetch, persist to localStorage while offline with a bounded queue, and replay automatically once your endpoint recovers.

pluginSystem.title: Hooks & plugins
pluginSystem.description: beforeSend / beforeSendBatch / afterSend / beforeBreadcrumb hooks for scrubbing, filtering and sampling; React and Vue adapters, Performance / ScreenRecord / Exposure plugins and an open plugin API.

features.footnote: Everything starts from one init() — each capture is one flag away from off, each plugin strictly opt-in.

workflow.description: No gateway, no SaaS account, no agent to deploy. Point the SDK at any endpoint that accepts JSON — or run the reference server and dashboard shipped in this repo.

install.title: Install
install.description: One package with ESM, CJS and type declarations; React, Vue, Vite and webpack integrations ship as separate subpath exports.

init.title: Initialize
init.description: Pass a dsn and capture starts — errors, HTTP, routing, page views and white-screen detection are on by default; vitals, replay and exposure are opt-in plugins.

insight.title: Insight
insight.description: Open your endpoint or the reference dashboard: crashes ranked, journeys replayed, vitals tracked.

install.description: Works with any bundler and any backend — if it can receive a POST, it can receive a report.
install.ctaTitle: Your users already hit the bug.
install.ctaBody: Add the SDK, deploy, and the next crash arrives with everything you need to fix it.

faq.bodyA: Anything else, open an issue on
faq.bodyB: — we usually reply within a day.

data.question: What does the SDK send?
data.answer: Only monitoring events: errors with stacks and breadcrumbs, failed HTTP requests, page views and dwell time, declarative clicks and exposures, performance metrics, white-screen events and — when a failure triggers it — a gzip-compressed screen recording. Everything goes only to the endpoint you set as your dsn.

size.question: How big is it?
size.answer: The core is a few kilobytes gzipped, with ESM, CJS and type declarations. Framework adapters, plugins and dev-server mocks live in separate subpath exports, and heavy dependencies like rrweb, pako and FingerprintJS are dynamically imported only when enabled.

frameworks.question: Which frameworks are supported?
frameworks.answer: Any vanilla JS app works out of the box. React ships an error boundary, Vue 3 a global error-handler plugin, and reportFrameworkError covers everything else. Vite and webpack dev-server plugins mock the report endpoint and resolve source maps during development.

privacy.question: Can I control what leaves the browser?
privacy.answer: Yes. The beforeSend, beforeSendBatch, afterSend and beforeBreadcrumb hooks let you inspect, redact or drop any payload before it hits the network; every capture has its own enable flag; ignoreErrors and excludeAPIs filter noise; sampling and fingerprint identity are configurable.

offline.question: What happens on flaky connections?
offline.answer: Events batch in memory and persist to localStorage while offline, capped at a maximum queue length. The reporter flushes via sendBeacon or fetch, probes your dsn for recovery after failures, and replays the cache when the network returns.

license.question: Is it open source?
license.answer: MIT. No account, no required SaaS — the SDK talks to your own endpoint, and the repo ships a reference ingest server you can self-host.

footer.description: Frontend monitoring for teams who would rather see bugs than hear about them.
